title: Targeting synergetic endothelial inflammation by inhibiting NFKB and JAK-STAT pathways
projectDescription: Multiple systemic vascular inflammatory disorders are associated with endothelial dysfunction and elevated levels of TNFα and IFNγ. Combined TNFα and IFNγ stimulation induces synergetic hyperinflammation in endothelial cells (ECs) through activation of the NFKB and JAK/STAT pathways. Here we assess how targeting these pathways affects EC inflammation. Using mass-spectrometry based proteomics, we investigate system-wide effects of TNFα- and IFNγ-stimulated Endothelial Colony Forming Cells (ECFCs) in combination with inhibitors targeting NFKB and JAK/STAT pathways. JAK1 inhibitor itacitinib blocked IFNγ-, but not TNFα-induced proteomic responses. IKK2/STAT3 inhibitor TPCA1 attenuated both responses. Most TNFα+IFNγ-induced proteins, such as pyroptosis mediators, chemokines and Weibel-Palade Body content, were inhibited by both inhibitors, highlighting their synergetic dependency on both pathways. Imaging of Von Willebrand Factor (VWF) revealed an extracellular VWF network induced by combined stimulation; a phenotype which was reverted by both inhibitors. This study provides a mechanistic basis for inhibiting endothelial inflammation in vascular inflammatory disorders.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Mass spectrometry analysis For mass spectrometry analysis of EC proteomes, cells were lysed and proteins were digested with trypsin as described previously(DOI: 10.1038/s42003-024-06649-w). Secretomes were processed the same, but SDC was omitted from the lysis buffer. Tryptic digests were transferred to an Evotip Pure (Evosep) according to manufactures guidelines and separated on a 8 cm × 150 μm, 1.5 μm Performance Column (EV1137 from EvoSep) with an Evosep One liquid chromatography (LC) system (Evosep) using the 60 samples per day gradient. The lysates and secretomes for 4,8, 24h time point experiment was analysed using the 30 samples per day gradient. Buffer A was composed of 0.1 % formic acid, buffer B of 0.1 % formic acid in acetonitrile (Biosolve, NLD). Peptides were ionized and electro sprayed into a TimsTOF HT mass spectrometer (Bruker). Data was acquired in diaPASEF mode, using an MS1 scan range of 100-1700 m/z. For MS2 acquisition 32 pyDIAID system-optimized55 windows were used, with a cycle time of 1.80 seconds and a mass and ion mobility range from 400.2-1500.8 m/z and 0.70-1.50 1/k0 respectively. Collision energy used was 20.00 eV at 0.6 1/k0 and 59 eV at 1.60 1/k0.
dataProcessingProtocol: Data analysis Raw mass spectrometry data files were processed using DIA-NN software (version 1.8.1)56, proteins and peptides were detected by querying the filtered human Swissprot database (release 2021.22.04). Standard settings were used, using a generated library-based spectra search. Maximum number of variable modifications was set at 2, protein interference as “Protein names (from FASTA)” and quantification strategy as “Robust LC (high accuracy)”.
